extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and PIs applying for NIH grants (R01/R21/R35/K99/SBIR/etc.), especially early-stage investigators
extracted.subtask_description: Practical advice on interpreting NIH application statuses, interacting with Program Officials and Grants Management Specialists, timing and logistics of funding decisions, resubmission strategy, and options for avoiding funding gaps for competing renewals and new awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact Program Officer to gauge funding likelihood and resubmission strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask your PO whether you should plan on resubmitting as a way of gauging your funding likelihood and soliciting input on strategies for resubmission (based on panel discussion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact the PO for advice on whether to prepare an A1 and for revision strategies; if the PO is unresponsive, escalate (see 'copy branch chief' guidance). Do not repeatedly push to 'speed up' funding decisions—POs are cautious and will avoid promising funding until Notices of Award are issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copy Branch Chief / escalate when PO is unresponsive
rubrics_metrics.description: If PO gives zero response, find the PO’s boss (Branch Chief) and cc: them on the email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use institutional directories (e.g., NED) to find contacts. Document communication and, if needed, elevate to branch chief, DER, or acting directors to get clarity — especially when lab personnel depend on the award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of 'Council review completed' status
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Council review completed’ is the status of every application (scored or not) after the IC Council meeting. It doesn’t mean anything specific about funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Council reviews peer review quality and mission alignment but does not make final funding decisions. Final decisions are by the IC Director after internal prioritization and administrative processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of Advisory Council/Board vs IC Director
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council's role is to review the quality of peer review and confirm that the science is within the IC’s mission, not to make funding decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Council approves en bloc a list of applications the IC Director may consider. The IC Director orders a paylist and makes final funding choices; internal post-Council meetings determine ordering and which outside-payline apps get considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: JIT requests indicate positive funding signal (but not guaranteed)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the GMS (or PO) requests JIT information, that would be a positive sign that the application is being considered for funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absence of a JIT request is neutral — some awards proceed using an earlier JIT or without a new request. Do not assume lack of JIT means no funding; likewise, JIT is not absolute confirmation until NoA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addition of Grants Management Specialist (GMS) in eRA Commons is suggestive but not definitive
rubrics_metrics.description: The addition of the GMS alone does not mean a lot, but combined with JIT requests or status changes it could be positive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor for accompanying administrative status changes or requests; reach out to PO/GMS only when appropriate — excessive inquiries are discouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payline and 'select pay' timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Select pay awards are typically funded at the end of the fiscal year (late summer) when ICs know how much discretionary money remains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cycle 2 decisions are often made in Feb–Apr; Cycle 1 is often delayed. Some applications outside the automatic payline may still be funded later if discretionary funds remain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early Stage Investigator (ESI) payline application of policy
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are an ESI you should get the ESI payline (policy applies to R01 equivalents); if your Summary Statement documents ESI status, you should be eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an IC appears to ignore ESI payline, point them to the IC payline policy website or discuss with your PO. Study section assignment or special review panels do not generally remove ESI consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare a resubmission (A1) while awaiting funding decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: It’s better to prepare the A1 and decide whether to submit later than to miss a cycle; doing extra work helps clarify the science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask the PO for timing advice, but starting revisions early avoids missing submission deadlines if funding does not come through. POs often advise conservatively; if they don’t encourage resubmission that is a positive sign.

rubrics_metrics.name: IC secondary assignment / transfer and co-funding considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: If a secondary IC (e.g., NIBIB) is interested, you can ask your primary IC PO about transferring the application — but the original IC may no longer consider it for funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfers require coordination between POs; ask whether co-funding or administrative IC transfer is feasible. Transfers late in the cycle are less likely and may remove the app from consideration by the original IC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling overlapping project periods/start dates for renewals
rubrics_metrics.description: When a renewal start date overlaps with an existing award end date, Institutes typically reduce the first year of the renewal by the amount carried over and set a new project period start date when the competing renewal starts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can ask your grant/fiscal administrator or GMS about negotiating a delayed start (e.g., to Sept) to avoid losing funds; institutions handle these situations routinely.

rubrics_metrics.name: NRFC (Not Recommended for Further Consideration) meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: NRFC grants are those that review panels rate so poorly that Council is forbidden from recommending them for funding; worse than Not Discussed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NRFC indicates applications with serious problems (e.g., pseudoscience); if you see NRFC language seek detailed feedback and do not resubmit without major changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: SRO timing for posting scores
rubrics_metrics.description: The Scientific Review Officer (SRO) has about 3 working days to input scores and release the meeting; timing to posting depends on workload, not score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delays in score posting are common and not predictive of outcome; ND (not discussed) and scored apps can post at similar times depending on SRO workload.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study section assignment appeals / who to contact
rubrics_metrics.description: If your application is assigned to a different study section than requested, contact the CSR website for the SRO or SRO’s boss; you must provide a strong scientific reason for reassignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final decision on study section assignment rests with CSR/SRO; contacting them early is appropriate if you have substantive cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-award spending is possible within ~90 days of expected award
rubrics_metrics.description: If you need to start purchases, ask your institution’s grant/fiscal administrator about setting up an account for pre-award spending since you may be within ~90 days of award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions commonly set up pre-award accounts; this reduces pressure to have immediate NoA but must be handled according to institutional policy and risk tolerance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Officers are conservative in resubmission advice
rubrics_metrics.description: POs tend to avoid advising PIs to 'wait' when funding is uncertain; they prefer recommending resubmission to avoid a PI missing a funding cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a PO does not recommend resubmission, that may indicate confidence in funding; conversely, lack of encouragement to wait should be interpreted cautiously and discussed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative 'pending' status and processing queue
rubrics_metrics.description: ICs process awards manually in a queue; status changes like 'pending administrative review' mean your application is in line for administrative processing and drafting of the Notice of Award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After administrative review and NoA drafting, the Institute Director must sign off; timing is variable and can be affected by broader events (e.g., federal budget delays, pandemics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of R56 or short-term bridge funding to avoid gaps
rubrics_metrics.description: If an IC can’t fund a renewal, consider negotiating R56 bridge funding or asking about co-funding from another IC to cover a transition while you prepare a new submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NICHD or another IC holding the application may be better positioned to issue short-term R56 funding; ask the PO to make personal referrals to other IC POs or consider requesting one-year bridge support.

rubrics_metrics.name: A1 outcomes do not automatically negate A0 funding
rubrics_metrics.description: A worse A1 score does not necessarily affect the funding outcome of an A0; ICs can ignore the A1 and fund the A0 if merited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat A0 and A1 as separate applications administratively; contact PO if you are concerned about the relationship between multiple submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document communications and timelines when contesting decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: If you believe an IC mishandled fit-to-mission or miscommunication led to lost funding opportunities, document the submission, review, and post-submission communications and consider escalating to the IC Director of Extramural Research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concise timeline and evidence (emails, phone notes). Escalation may be appropriate for ESI renewals or cases where institutional disruption (layoffs) results from administrative decisions.
